channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Em campanha simultânea no Rio, Lula defende prender criminosos; e Flávio fala em ‘guerra’ ao crime
item.description: Lula promises to arrest criminals and return territories to the people, while Flávio Bolsonaro declares war on narcoterrorists starting in 2027. Both held simultaneous campaigns in Rio advocating public security policies.

item.title: Caiado chama adversários de 'fujões' e 'amarelões' por provável ausência em debate presidencial
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado criticized the likely absence of opponents in presidential debates, calling them cowards and yellows. He claimed that candidates who do not participate are running, turning yellow, and chickening out, suggesting they avoid public discussion.

item.title: Lula e Renan têm mais voto por propostas, Flávio depende mais da rejeição
item.description: Datafolha polling on the 2026 presidential race shows Lula and Renan Cânbio rely more on vote-by-conviction based on proposals, while Flávio Bolsonaro depends more on voter rejection of opponents. A sizable voting bloc remains intent on preventing someone's victory, indicating persistent polarization.

item.title: De colete à prova de balas, Renan Santos vai a comunidade em SP e promete programa de R$ 1,5 trilhão contra favelização
item.description: Renan Santos, presidential candidate from Missão, visited the Jardim Panorama community in São Paulo and proposed a slum-upgrading program with investments between R$1.3 and R$1.5 trillion. The plan includes housing renovation, property regularization, and expanded public services, without relocating residents. Funding will come from public and private sources, expense cuts, and tax exemptions.

item.title: Lula acena a religiosos e defende tirar o RJ das "páginas policiais"
item.description: Lula held his first campaign rally in Rio de Janeiro, focusing on public security and combating organized crime. He advocated moving the state from 'police pages' to 'political pages,' promising arrests without violence and returning territory to the people. The speech included strategic appeals to religiosity and references to God.

item.title: Lula promete “revolução energética” para sediar data centers
item.description: Lula promises an energy revolution focused on renewables to attract data centers, highlighting Brazil's potential in wind, solar, and green hydrogen. He advocates for the approval of the Redata tax exemption bill and mentioned other priorities like AI in Portuguese and public safety.

item.title: Lula diz que campanhas usarão IA porque rivais “não sabem a verdade”
item.description: Lula criticized the use of AI by his political opponents, claiming they lack commitment to truth and resort to technology to manipulate images and generate false content. He warned that the 2026 campaign will see extensive use of AI to distort reality, particularly targeting candidates like Eduardo Paes. The speech was delivered at a campaign rally in Rio de Janeiro, attended by allies and supporters of his re-election bid.

item.title: As metas ambiciosas do PL para as eleições à Câmara e ao Senado
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's PL party has set ambitious electoral targets for the upcoming elections: elect 105 federal deputies and increase its Senate caucus from 16 to 26 members. The strategy aims to strengthen the party in Congress and secure influence in the Legislative Branch, with potential plans to elect a Senate president if Bolsonaro wins the presidency.

item.title: Planos de governo de Lula e Flávio prometem seguro e crédito ao agro
item.description: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro agree on expanding rural credit and insurance to combat 8.8% farm default rates. Lula emphasizes a record R$ 525 billion Safra Plan and catastrophic loss insurance, while Flávio proposes debt securitization and storage expansion. Both treat agribusiness as strategic, though Lula highlights family farming.

item.title: Lula volta a prometer Ministério da Segurança e reforça aliança com Paes em ato de campanha no Rio
item.description: Lula pledged to create a Ministry of Public Security during a campaign rally in Rio, reinforcing his alliance with Eduardo Paes. He advocated for a constitutional amendment to strengthen federal police forces, promising to reclaim territories from criminals and return them to the people.

item.title: Lula diz não querer guerra, mas investirá em Defesa: 'Não se metam conosco'
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated in Bangu, in the west zone of Rio de Janeiro, that he does not want war with any country, but intends to invest in Defense to prepare the country. In a warning tone, he declared 'Don't mess with us', signaling a stance of military strengthening.

item.title: Lula defende candidatura de Paes ao governo do Rio: 'É uma necessidade para o povo'
item.description: President Lula endorsed this Saturday the candidacy of former mayor Eduardo Paes for the governorship of Rio de Janeiro, calling it 'a necessity for the people'. The statement was made amid the 2026 electoral process, reinforcing the PT's support for an ally from PSD in the state of Rio.

item.title: Em evento na capital paulista, Tarcísio defende ampliação do metrô a novas regiões
item.description: São Paulo governor Tarcísio de Freitas stated that the state plans to expand transportation and specialized services in the capital. At an event alongside mayor Ricardo Nunes, he pledged to extend the metro to new areas and create more TEA Centers and Atypical Mother Houses.

item.title: Eduardo Paes: Lula e eu temos desejo de salvar o RJ. Brasil não se salva se RJ não se salvar
item.description: Eduardo Paes (PSD), candidate for governor of Rio de Janeiro, joined President Lula (PT) at a campaign event and stated they share the desire to save the state. According to Paes, Brazil cannot be saved without Rio de Janeiro also being saved, highlighting the alliance between the two for the 2026 elections.

item.title: Crime organizado “sentou” no Palácio Guanabara, diz Eduardo Paes
item.description: Former Rio mayor Eduardo Paes (PSD) said at a campaign event alongside President Lula that organized crime has 'taken over' the Guanabara Palace, criticizing former governor Cláudio Castro's (PL) administration. Paes cited Operation Ouroboros, which investigates the diversion of R$86.3 million from the Rio Metrópole Institute, and listed Castro's former secretaries arrested for links to organized crime. He also referenced opponent Rodrigo Bacellar (União Brasil), now imprisoned and ineligible, as another example of the state's crisis.

item.title: “Alguém aqui mora em Palácio?”, diz Flávio após Lula criticar Alvorada
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro mocked Lula at a Rio rally, criticizing the president's complaints about the Alvorada Palace. The senator contrasted the 'Palace elite' with the 'streets', also attacking rival Eduardo Paes, and emphasized his humble roots in Tijuca.

item.title: Celina promete reformar UPAs, hospitais e dar reajuste para médicos
item.description: Governor of the Federal District, Celina Leão (PP), running for re-election, presented health proposals including salary increases for doctors, renovations of UPAs and hospitals, delivery of new units, and the hiring of 500 medical professionals. She countered criticism from rival José Roberto Arruda (PSD) by referencing past health failures. She also highlighted initiatives to assist homeless people in Brasília's Plano Piloto.

item.title: "Gostaria de vê-los", diz Tarcísio sobre Lula e Flávio fora de debate
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicans), running for reelection, said he would like to see President Lula (PT) and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) at the presidential debate scheduled for Sunday (August 23), which both have said they will skip. Tarcísio attributed their absence to electoral strategies tied to polling positions but argued voters need to hear candidates' plans. He also reaffirmed his support for Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential bid, citing concerns about Brazil's fiscal situation.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro repete bravatas sobre ‘narcoterroristas’ e pede anistia para Jair e outros golpistas
item.description: Presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) repeated his proposal to label the Comando Vermelho and PCC as 'narco-terrorists' during an event in Rio de Janeiro, threatening to 'declare war' on these factions from January 2027 onward if elected. He also once again defended amnesty for those involved in the January 8, 2023 coup attempts, including his father, Jair Bolsonaro. The measure aligns with the US position, while the Lula government fears legal and sovereignty implications.

item.title: No RJ, Lula diz que, se reeleito, vai retirar facções e devolver território ao povo
item.description: Lula pledges, if reelected, to remove criminal factions from Rio de Janeiro and return territories to the people, citing the Public Security PEC and the recreation of the Ministry of Public Security. The president made the announcement at a campaign rally in Rio's West Zone alongside allies like Eduardo Paes and Benedita da Silva, aiming to improve his security approval ratings and appeal to evangelicals.

item.title: Zema lança jingle com vídeo que mostra Lula e ministros do STF presos
item.description: Romeu Zema, the Novo party's presidential candidate, released a campaign jingle advocating to 'end the PT.' The song is a parody of Gabriel Diniz's 'O nome dela é Jennifer,' accompanied by an AI-generated video depicting President Lula and Supreme Court ministers in jail.

item.title: Tarcísio diz que estará com Flávio e quer vê-lo no debate com Lula
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicans) declared his support for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) in the presidential race during a campaign event in São Bernardo do Campo. Tarcísio said he would like to see Flávio and President Lula in debates, regretting both candidates' absence from Band's first presidential debate. The governor also emphasized that his administration operates with pragmatism, regardless of partisan alignment.

item.title: “O bandido será tirado de circulação, em pé ou deitado”, diz Flávio
item.description: Presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) stated at a rally in Rio de Janeiro's Maracanãzinho that criminals will be taken off the streets 'standing or lying down' if elected, pledging to classify PCC, Comando Vermelho, and militias as terrorist groups and to wage war on 'narcoterrorists.' His proposals include a minimum 8-year sentence for cell phone theft, chemical castration for rapists, and lowering the age of criminal responsibility to 14 in rape cases. He also vowed to maintain Bolsa Família while adding professional qualification measures and promoting his Minha Primeira Empresa entrepreneurship program.

item.title: Flávio sobre combate ao crime: Bandido será tirado de circulação em pé ou deitado
item.description: Presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) reiterated this Saturday (22) his proposal for a tougher crime-fighting approach. In a controversial statement, he said that 'criminals will be taken off the streets, standing or lying down,' likely referring to the killing of criminals. The remarks reinforce the hardline stance the candidate has adopted on public security.

item.title: Em ato com Lula, Paes diz que o "crime sentou no Palácio Guanabara"
item.description: At a campaign rally in Rio alongside President Lula, gubernatorial candidate Eduardo Paes (PSD) claimed organized crime has taken over the Guanabara Palace and called for unity to "save" the state, citing Federal Police investigations against rivals. Paes leads the Rio governor race with 41% of voting intentions in the first round versus 19% for Douglas Ruas (PL), according to a Datafolha poll. The event also featured Senate candidates Benedita da Silva (PT) and Pedro Paulo (PSD).

item.title: Haddad diz que Datafolha está ‘meio esquisito’ e que desconhece quatro candidatos citados pela pesquisa
item.description: Fernando Haddad criticized Datafolha, calling it 'a bit weird' and stating he does not recognize four candidates mentioned in the survey. The poll shows Tarcisio de Freitas leading with 45%, followed by Haddad with 27%. At the launch of his Education program, Haddad promised new public school teacher competitions and reinforced full-time education.

item.title: Haddad chama de ‘esquisito’ Datafolha que mostra Tarcísio 18 pontos à frente em São Paulo
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT) called the Datafolha poll 'strange' as it shows Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicans) leading the São Paulo governor race by 18 points, with 45% versus 27%. The former minister questioned the survey citing four unknown candidates totaling 9%, but acknowledged that PT internal trackings also show a 'reasonably large' advantage for his opponent. In a runoff, Tarcísio would win 54% to 35%.

item.title: No Rio, Flávio promete enquadrar milícias, PCC e CV como terroristas
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), during a Rio event launching Douglas Ruas's gubernatorial bid, pledged to label the PCC, Red Command, and militias as terrorist organizations, pushing a hardline anti-crime agenda. The proposal clashes with the Lula administration's refusal of a similar US designation, citing risks of foreign military action on Brazilian soil. Public security has emerged as a cornerstone of Flávio's presidential campaign, resonating with voter priorities shown in recent polls.

item.title: Haddad minimiza números do Datafolha e diz confiar em dados do PT
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT) downplayed election polls showing Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) leading by a large margin, saying he trusts his party's internal data. At an education event, he proposed more full-time schools, teacher salary increases, and the creation of CEUs. He criticized Tarcísio's administration, opposing civic-military schools and the outsourcing of state schools.

item.title: Janja pede que mulheres falem dos feitos de Lula para angariar votos
item.description: First lady Janja Lula da Silva urged women at a political rally in Bangu, Rio de Janeiro's west zone, to mobilize their networks—friends, neighbors, and coworkers—to spread the word about President Lula's achievements and secure votes for the 2026 election. The event brought together President Lula, mayor Eduardo Paes, and Senate candidates, emphasizing women's public policies and outreach to female voters.

item.title: Tarcísio diz que queria ver Lula e Flávio no debate: 'Cidadăo demanda'
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicans), governor of São Paulo, lamented the absence of Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro from the Band debate, stating that citizens have the right to see the candidates presenting their plans for the country. The absence of the two pre-candidates was criticized as harmful to the democratic process and to voters' choice.

item.title: Cavaliere exalta parceria do Rio com Lula e diz que Paes pode reconstruir o Estado
item.description: Rio de Janeiro Mayor Eduardo Cavaliere (PSD) praised the partnership between the city and the Lula government, stating that the alliance has delivered numerous advances to the municipality. Cavaliere also suggested that Eduardo Paes has the potential to rebuild the State of Rio. The remarks highlight the political coordination between Rio's PSD and the federal administration.

item.title: Flávio diz que narcoterroristas têm até dezembro para ‘meter o pé’ do Brasil e promete ‘guerra’ contra criminosos
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, PL presidential candidate, vowed to designate criminal factions like Comando Vermelho and PCC as narcoterrorist groups and wage 'war' against them starting January. He also supports amnesty for January 8 perpetrators, lowering the age of criminal responsibility in rape cases, and chemical castration for rapists.

item.title: “Já pode chamar de genocida?”, questiona Flávio sobre Lula
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro criticized President Lula by sharing a Veja report on indigenous deaths in the Yanomami Territory, asking if he can now be called a genocide. The post reignited debate over violence against indigenous peoples under the current administration.

item.title: Lula e Flávio fazem atos de campanha no RJ neste sábado
item.description: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro held campaign events in Rio de Janeiro, with Lula at the Moça Bonita stadium and Flávio at the Maracanãzinho. Datafolha poll shows them within the margin of error, with 39% and 33% in voter intentions, respectively.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro lista propostas de segurança pública em ato com presença de Ruas e apelo às mulheres no Rio
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro launched public security proposals at an event in Rio, promising to declare war on factions like CV and PCC, approve chemical castration for rapists, and increase prison sentences for crimes such as cellphone theft. Douglas Ruas and Eduardo Pazuello also spoke, appealing to the female electorate and criticizing previous governments. The event aimed to mobilize the PL base ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: No RJ, Flávio defende anistia, castração química e o Bolsa Família
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) defended amnesty for January 8 convicts, chemical castration for rapists, and maintaining Bolsa Família at the launch event for Douglas Ruas's (PL) Rio de Janeiro gubernatorial candidacy. Eduardo Pazuello (PL) stated women voters will decide the 2026 elections. Datafolha poll shows Eduardo Paes (PSD) leading with 41% versus 19% for Douglas Ruas.

item.title: Zema divulga jingle que em que promete 'acabar com PT' e mostra Lula e ministros do STF atrás das grades
item.description: Romeu Zema, the Novo Party's presidential candidate, released a campaign jingle promising to end the PT while depicting Lula, Gilmar Mendes, and Alexandre de Moraes as prisoners. The AI-produced piece criticizes the STF, 'jogo do tigrinho', Virgínia Fonseca, and issues like improper INSS discounts and rising food prices.

item.title: Tarcísio sobre ausência de Flávio e Lula em debate: 'Questão de estratégia'
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas described the absence of Flávio Bolsonaro and Lula da Silva from the Band/Estadão presidential debate as an electoral strategy. The São Paulo governor and reelection candidate made the statement after the event was canceled for both candidates.

item.title: Candidato ao governo do Rio, Ruas diz que mulheres 'vão decidir futuro do Brasil'
item.description: Douglas Ruas (PL) emphasized women's role in deciding Brazil's future and pledged to prioritize protection and autonomy for women in his administration.

item.title: Sebastião Coelho se diz "injustiçado" após atrito com Malafaia
item.description: Retired judge Sebastião Coelho (Novo), Senate candidate for the Federal District, says he feels wronged after Pastor Silas Malafaia warned that a divided right risks electing a left-wing senator and called him a "cretin." Coelho vows to continue his candidacy, registered July 21, and says he declined offers to be running mate for Michelle Bolsonaro (PL) and Bia Kicis (PL) due to his party commitment.

item.title: Douglas Ruas cita Madonna e diz que sua gestão terá "show da saúde"
item.description: Douglas Ruas criticized the Todo Mundo no Rio event and promised a 'show of health and security' in his government, contrasting it with celebrity shows like Madonna. He emphasized inclusive policies and attacked opponents, including Eduardo Paes.

item.title: Caso Lulinha: gabinete de Mendonça rebate suspeitas e defende investigação de vazamentos
item.description: The office of Supreme Court Minister André Mendonça rejected suspicions that the Lulinha case data leaks originated from the court itself. Lawyers for lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger requested the investigation be expanded to include agents with access to the case, such as two police delegates working in Mendonça's office, one of whom has tensions with the PF leadership. The office denied that the agents participated in anti-fascist dossiers or investigations, emphasizing Mendonça's support for probing the leaks.

item.title: O encontro de Messias e Alcolumbre na posse de Salomão no STJ
item.description: At the ceremony for Luís Felipe Salomão's swearing-in as STJ president, AGU minister Jorge Messias and Senate president Davi Alcolumbre met but did not speak. The tension stems from Messias's failed nomination to the STF, a defeat blamed on Alcolumbre, who briefly broke with Lula. Although Lula and Alcolumbre have resumed dialogue, Messias has not yet reconciled with the Senate president.

item.title: Haddad promete mudar uso de plataformas digitais nas escolas de SP: 'Esse terror vai acabar'
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT) promised to change the use of digital platforms in São Paulo state schools on his first day in office, criticizing the policy of Governor Tarcísio de Freitas. He also announced new public exams for teachers and advocated for greater pedagogical autonomy, supported by Marina Silva and Simone Tebet.

item.title: Careca do INSS sobre amiga de Lulinha: ‘Tá na folha? Tem que resolver’
item.description: The Federal Police investigate Careca do INSS for embezzling 6 billion reais and his influence on the government through Lulinha, President Lula's son. Messages reveal pressure to approve businesses involving cannabidiol-based medicines and payroll loan discounts, with lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger acting as an intermediary.

item.title: Zema busca apoio de juristas evangélicos para tentar se aproximar do eleitorado religioso
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) has established a nucleus to engage the evangelical electorate, led by Uziel Santana, founder of Anajure. Santana views Zema as an alternative to Flávio Bolsonaro, though polls show the candidate has only 2% support among evangelicals.

item.title: Lula diz que sugeriu a Trump um “trago” com Xi e Putin depois da ONU
item.description: Lula suggested to Trump an informal meeting with Xi and Putin to seek peace in international conflicts, highlighting his concern about wars. During the call, Trump acknowledged that tariffs on Brazilian products were based on incorrect information, agreeing to advance trade negotiations. Lula also proposed cooperation between Brazil and the U.S. against organized crime, rejecting foreign interference.

item.title: Flávio dá nome de “Chiquinho” a cachorro que ganhou em ato no RJ
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) named 'Chiquinho' the dog rescued from animal abuse who was given to him during his campaign launch in Copacabana, Rio de Janeiro. The adoption was suggested by supporters and the name was chosen by his daughters. The event was used to associate the campaign with the law signed by Jair Bolsonaro that increased penalties for animal abuse.

item.title: PL tenta evitar voto casado em Flávio e Paes e aposta em ataques ao candidato do PSD
item.description: The PL party in Rio de Janeiro holds a campaign launch event for Douglas Ruas and uses the occasion to attack Eduardo Paes (PSD) to prevent the 'Flávio-Paes' split vote. The strategy involves linking Paes to Lula and Sérgio Cabral, as well as reviving the 'Nervosinho' nickname linked to Odebrecht. A Datafolha poll shows Paes leading with 41%, with Ruas in second place at 19%.
